title: Interlude audio acceptance and implementation
summary: Defines mandatory world-audio acceptance for 1:1 Interlude parity: sequencing, per-actor audio bundles, source-export coverage, runtime ownership, and evidence rules.
scope: human class skills and special attacks
ambient sound objects and PointRegion metadata
notes: Manifest-declared SPEC (manifest_override true, precedence 7). Owner, dated and work-order statements recorded for conflict detection: (1) Intro: 'The user's 2026-11-06 clarification makes audio mandatory for 1:1.' (2) 'Current sequencing and system bundles - 2026-11-07': 'Finish human male/female, their class skills and usable 20_20 traversal before more races or tiles.' (3) Same section: 'Audio is part of each actor, animation, skill and enemy dependency bundle, not a later optional project.' (4) Same section: 'Preserve the completed 4,773-sound corpus receipts; do not repeat that batch to connect a selected actor or skill.' (5) Intro: 'The browser implementation owner owns end-to-end integration and coordinates source research. Terrain work and its existing protections remain in force.' (6) 'Runtime ownership and delivery': 'No service changes, deployment, publication or new native runtime/capture action is authorized by this clarification alone.' (7) 'Runtime ownership and delivery': the terrain-pilot owner holds one supervised apitrace 14.0 win32 graphics-pilot authorization on IMPORTA-PC, which adds no audio capture or native configuration permission. (8) 'Required coverage': 'Use the current hash-identified Interlude client on IMPORTA-PC.' (9) 'Evidence required to pass': 'Define timing/amplitude/spatial tolerances and a single measured alignment method before parity implementation/comparison.' Numerical audio tolerances are stated as unestablished, so native audio parity cannot pass. Document also sets 'Overall 1:1 remains incomplete while world audio or any required category is missing or unverified.' Several dated checkpoints (2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07) describe counts that supersede each other; the doc says they must not be summed. Sections 'Historical extraction/inspector boundary' and the 2026-11-06 census are explicitly historical.
